parts.label: Part 2
parts.article:
Next week is our town's International Week, which has been going on annually for several years. Today we have George Johnson, the organizer of International Week, to talk about it. George, how did it all begin?

Well, I was with a group of businessmen in town one February day five years ago. And we were discussing what we could do for livening things up in August when the weather is good and the kids are out of school till September. And someone said, hey, we've got people from all over the world living here. Let's have an international Celebration and get people to show off things about their home country. And we all agreed the first year the Celebration lasted just one day and it featured three countries. It was a great success and was written about in our local newspaper. And so the next year, even though it costs more, the organizers expanded it to an international week. And so many people were eager to feature their countries on each of the first six days of the week, one country is designated to star.

And then on the seventh day, weather permitting, we have a street party near the town hall with music provided by the radio station and food and games. Everyone has a ball. Of course, we move it to the school gym if it rains like last year, but nobody minds.

Our year starts in January when we ask for applications. To apply to have a day for their country, people don't need to belong to a particular country association. They can just be a group who identified themselves with a particular country. They submit a formal plan to us. They don't need to worry at this stage about funding, but some grants are available. The organizing committee has to select the ones with the best ideas.

The organizing committee arranges for places for the country to do whatever they want. Unfortunately, for large outdoor activities, we aren't allowed to use the local stadium because they've got other commitments. But the community center lets us use its parking lot. The hall is kind of small, but it has been kind enough to permit us to make use of its classrooms. Local people have been very generous. A lot of business people let us have things like tables and amplifiers for the week. The organizing committee handles all the administration and the town library has been great about featuring books about the countries.

Now for each country's day, we ask him to have one special event like a show or exhibition or demonstration. For example, some people could show how they make traditional handicrafts, or it might just be an exhibition, say photographs of the country.

Interesting. Now, what are. Are the special events this year.

Fantastic things. Monday is Mexico Day, and these ladies and gentlemen are going to put on a show that's hotter than those chilli peppers they're famous for eating. They'll be singing and playing songs. And those drums will make you want to get up and move around.

Then Tuesday is South Africa Day, and they've got an exhibition of dresses and robes used in traditional ceremonies and dances. And they are magnificent. Apparently, some of them are worth more than their weight in gold.

Next Wednesday is Indonesia Day. They have an exhibition where you'll definitely get your money's worth. Two ladies will put on their chef's hat to demonstrate how they prepare those dishes and sauces they're famous for. Let's see.

That brings us to Thursday, Canada Day. We think of them as fit outdoorsman and ice hockey players. But they've arranged to have some of their countrymen show us how they use just a knife and blocks of wood from Native American trees to make absolutely lovely statues of birds and bears and other animals famous in local legends. So next is Friday, Italy Day.

questions.question: Why did they change the celebration from one day to a week?

analyses.content: And we all agreed the first year the Celebration lasted just one day and it featured three countries. It was a great success and was written about in our local newspaper. And so the next year, even though it costs more, the organizers expanded it to an international week. And so many people were eager to feature their countries on each of the first six days of the week, one country is designated to star.
你可能会选选项C（人们想展示自己的国家），因为后面听到了“people were eager to feature their countries”，但这已经是活动变成“国际周”之后大家的参与热情了，并不是最初决定扩长时间的原因。
录音里提到第一年的活动很成功并被当地报纸报道了（written about in our local newspaper），因此（And so）第二年才扩大成了一周的规模。

analyses.content: And then on the seventh day, weather permitting, we have a street party near the town hall with music provided by the radio station and food and games. Everyone has a ball. Of course, we move it to the school gym if it rains like last year, but nobody minds.

录音直接给出了结果，说明如果像去年一样下雨，就会把活动移到学校体育馆（school gym）。

录音明确说到，社区中心允许他们使用其停车场（parking lot）来办大型户外活动。
